title: Mae Moh Half Marathon 2026 Review: A Utility Company's Race Near Its Own Mine
seo_title: Mae Moh Half Marathon 2026 Review | Lampang, Thailand
meta_description: Mae Moh Half Marathon 2026 review: October 25, organised by Thailand's EGAT power utility near the largest lignite mine in Southeast Asia.
dek: Set for 25 October 2026 in Mae Moh, Lampang, this race is organised by the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand -- the same utility that runs the massive Mae Moh coal power plant and lignite mine nearby.
verdict: The Mae Moh Half Marathon has an unusual organisational identity: it's run directly by EGAT, the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand -- the state utility that operates the 2,625MW Mae Moh Power Plant and the adjacent Mae Moh lignite mine, the largest coal mine in Thailand and the largest lignite mine in Southeast Asia. That's a genuinely distinctive sponsor profile, similar in spirit to the railway-backed Locomotive Half Marathon covered elsewhere in this research -- a national utility running a community race near its own major infrastructure, rather than a sportswear or beverage brand.

sections.heading: Organised by a National Power Utility
paragraphs: The race is organised by the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT), offering three distances: 21.1K, 10K and 5K in Mae Moh, Lampang. [1] EGAT is Thailand's state power utility -- and notably, it operates the Mae Moh Power Plant directly adjacent to the race venue, giving the event a genuinely unusual industrial-utility sponsorship model rather than a typical consumer brand.

sections.heading: Next to Southeast Asia's Largest Lignite Mine
paragraphs: Mae Moh Power Plant is a 2,625MW coal-fired facility that began operation in 1978, with its opening ceremony performed by King Bhumibol Adulyadej in 1985. [2] Fuel comes from the adjacent Mae Moh lignite mine, which is the largest coal mine in Thailand and the largest lignite mine in all of Southeast Asia. Running a half marathon in this immediate vicinity gives the race a genuinely industrial backdrop unlike any other event in this research batch.

sections.heading: A Real Point of Institutional Credibility
paragraphs: EGAT's direct organisational role suggests genuine logistical and financial resources behind the event, similar to how bank-backed races (VPBank, Techcombank, Malioboro Run's Bank BPD DIY) covered elsewhere in this research carry institutional weight beyond a typical commercial promoter. [1]

sections.heading: Registration Not Yet Announced
paragraphs: As of this writing, registration status has not been announced. [1] No independent participant reviews were found for this event, though it's listed across multiple aggregators including AIMS World Running and Thai.run.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If a genuinely unusual, utility-backed race near one of Southeast Asia's largest coal mining operations appeals -- and you're comfortable with an industrial rather than scenic backdrop -- the Mae Moh Half Marathon on 25 October 2026 offers something distinct from the region's more typical race destinations. Watch for registration to open before finalising travel.
